You are working in /home/user/fortress (the Fortress language revival repo, git branch claude/handover-reading-vn8zgr). Your job: try to build PDFs from the LaTeX sources in this repo, and report exactly what works. DO NOT commit anything, DO NOT push, DO NOT modify tracked files unless a build requires a trivial fix (report any such edit prominently). Build outputs should land wherever the build system puts them naturally; report the paths.

Targets, in priority order:
1. The language specification: `Specification/fortress/` has a build.xml (ant-driven LaTeX build, untested in this revival). There is also `Specification-1.0-frozen/`. Note both trees already contain a committed `fortress.1.0.pdf` — check (pdfinfo or strings) what date/version those PDFs are. The goal is a fresh build of `Specification/` (believed richer than the published 1.0 PDF).
2. `Papers/Dispatch/` (3 .tex files — identify what paper this is: title, authors, venue if determinable from the source).
3. `Documentation/Specification/` (5 .tex files — identify what this is; may be a spec fragment).
4. Sweep for any other buildable standalone documents with TeX sources in the repo (there's a stray `help.tex` and `latex-common/` at root) — identify them but only build if quick.

Environment notes:
- You may need to install LaTeX: `apt-get install -y texlive-latex-extra texlive-fonts-recommended` (add more packages only as errors demand; texlive-full is too big — disk is a fixed allowance, be frugal). `ant` is at /usr/bin/ant. If ant needs Java: export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64 and PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH, and `unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` first.
- The spec build may be driven by the root build.xml target `spec` or by `ant` inside Specification/fortress/ — read Specification/fortress/build.xml first to learn the entry point and expected TeX toolchain (it's 2007-2012 era: latex/pdflatex/bibtex/makeindex; missing .sty files are likely — latex-common/ dirs hold project styles).
- 2007-era LaTeX often breaks on modern texlive. Diagnose and apply minimal workarounds (e.g., missing style packages via apt, TEXINPUTS paths). If a document is genuinely unbuildable on modern texlive without deep surgery, say so precisely: first error, what it would take.

Report back (your final message is data for me, not for the user): per target — built OK or not, output PDF path + page count, what toolchain packages you installed, any source edits made, what the committed fortress.1.0.pdf turned out to be (date/producer), identification of the Dispatch paper and Documentation/Specification, and any other TeX documents found. Keep the report compact and factual.

<project name="FortressSpec" default="spec">
  <description>
    The Fortress specification, written in LaTeX.
  </description>

  <property environment="env"/>
  <property name="fortress.home"
            value="${env.FORTRESS_HOME}"/>
  <property name="compiler.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/ProjectFortress"/>
  <property name="example.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/SpecData/examples"/>
  <property name="preliminaries.example.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/SpecData/examples/preliminaries"/>
  <property name="basic.example.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/SpecData/examples/basic"/>
  <property name="advanced.example.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/SpecData/examples/advanced"/>
  <property name="library.example.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/SpecData/examples/library"/>
  <property name="library.api.home"
            value="${fortress.home}/Library"/>
  <property name="library.builtin.home"
            value="${compiler.home}/LibraryBuiltin"/>
  <property name="preliminaries.ex" value="${basedir}/../preliminaries/examples"/>
  <property name="basic.ex"         value="${basedir}/../basic/examples"/>
  <property name="advanced.ex"      value="${basedir}/../advanced/examples"/>
  <property name="library.ex"       value="${basedir}/../library/examples"/>
  <property name="library.api"      value="${basedir}/../library/apis"/>
  <property name="texinputs"        value=".:${fortress.home}/Fortify:"/>
  <property name="compiler.classpath"
            value="${compiler.home}/build:${compiler.home}/third_party/xtc/xtc.jar:${compiler.home}/third_party/jsr166y/jsr166y.jar:${compiler.home}/third_party/plt/plt.jar:${compiler.home}/third_party/junit/junit.jar"/>

  <taskdef name="fortress"
           classname="com.sun.fortress.ant_tasks.FortressTask"
	   classpath="${compiler.classpath}"/>

  <taskdef name="fortex"
           classname="com.sun.fortress.ant_tasks.FortexTask"
           classpath="${compiler.classpath}"/>

  <taskdef name="foreg"
           classname="com.sun.fortress.ant_tasks.ForegTask"
           classpath="${compiler.classpath}"/>

  <target name="spec" depends="genSource, makeExs, bib">
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
  </target>

  <target name="tex" depends="makeReservedWordsFiles, bib">
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
  </target>

  <target name="onlyTex">
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
  </target>

  <target name="bib">
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
    <exec executable="bibtex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
    <exec executable="pdflatex" failonerror="true">
      <arg value="fortress"/>
      <env key="TEXINPUTS" value="${texinputs}" />
    </exec>
  </target>

  <target name="genSource" depends="makeReservedWordsFiles, texExs"/>

  <target name="makeReservedWordsFiles">
    <exec executable="perl" dir="${basedir}">
      <arg value="keywords.pl"/>
    </exec>
    <exec executable="perl" dir="${basedir}">
      <arg value="unitOperators.pl"/>
    </exec>
    <exec executable="perl" dir="${basedir}">
      <arg value="specialReservedWords.pl"/>
    </exec>
  </target>

  <target name="texExs">
    <foreg>
      <fileset dir="${example.home}">
        <include name="**/*.fss"/>
        <include name="**/*.fsi"/>
      </fileset>
    </foreg>

    <fortex>
      <fileset dir="${library.api.home}">
        <include name="*.fsi"/>
      </fileset>
    </fortex>

    <fortex>
      <fileset dir="${library.builtin.home}">
        <include name="*.fsi"/>
      </fileset>
    </fortex>

    <move todir="${preliminaries.ex}">
      <fileset dir="${preliminaries.example.home}" includes="**/*.tex"/>
    </move>
    <move todir="${basic.ex}">
      <fileset dir="${basic.example.home}" includes="**/*.tex"/>
    </move>
    <move todir="${advanced.ex}">
      <fileset dir="${advanced.example.home}" includes="**/*.tex"/>
    </move>
    <move todir="${library.ex}">
      <fileset dir="${library.example.home}" includes="**/*.tex"/>
    </move>
    <move todir="${library.api}">
      <fileset dir="${library.api.home}" includes="*.tex"/>
      <fileset dir="${library.builtin.home}" includes="*.tex"/>
    </move>
  </target>

  <target name="makeExs" depends="texExs, evalExs, compileApis, evalLibExs"/>

  <target name="evalExs">
    <fortress>
      <env key="JAVA_FLAGS" value="-Xmx768m" />
      <fileset dir="${example.home}">
        <include name="**/*.fss"/>
        <exclude name="**/*.compile.fss"/>
        <exclude name="**/library/*.fss"/>
      </fileset>
    </fortress>
  </target>

  <target name="compileApis">
    <fortress compile="yes">
      <fileset dir="${example.home}">
        <include name="**/*.fsi"/>
        <include name="**/*.compile.fss"/>
        <exclude name="**/library/*.fss"/>
      </fileset>
    </fortress>
  </target>

  <target name="evalLibExs">
    <fortress parse="yes">
      <fileset dir="${library.example.home}">
        <include name="**/*.fss"/>
        <include name="**/*.fsi"/>
      </fileset>
    </fortress>
  </target>

  <target name="clean"
          description="Delete the generated files.">
    <delete file="fortress-keywords.tex"/>
    <delete file="fortress-unitOperators.tex"/>
    <delete file="fortress-specialReservedWords.tex"/>
    <delete>
      <fileset defaultexcludes="no" dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*~" />
      <fileset defaultexcludes="no" dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*#" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.log" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.dvi" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.ps" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.pdf" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.aux" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.toc" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.bbl" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.blg" />
      <fileset dir="${basedir}" includes="**/*.out" />
      <fileset dir="${preliminaries.ex}" includes="**/*.tex" />
      <fileset dir="${basic.ex}"         includes="**/*.tex" />
      <fileset dir="${advanced.ex}"      includes="**/*.tex" />
      <fileset dir="${library.ex}"       includes="**/*.tex" />
      <fileset dir="${library.api}"      includes="**/*.tex" />
    </delete>
  </target>

</project>
This directory contains the master file for the Fortress language
specification, along with an accompanying build script, helper scripts,
and some machine-generated helper files. 

To build the specification, call, you must have Ant installed, and you must 
set FORTRESS_HOME, so that Ant can locate the interpreter, fortify
tool, and libraries. Once FORTRESS_HOME is set, you can build the spec
by typing "./ant tex". Doing so will cause all machine-generated
helper files to be regenerated, and for the specification to be
recompiled. 

To regenerate all machine-generated files, without recompiling the
spec, call "./ant genSource".

## Report

**Environment/toolchain installed:** `texlive-latex-extra`, `texlive-fonts-recommended` (apt), `texlive-science` (apt, for `algpseudocode.sty`), `emacs-nox` (apt — `bin/fortick`/`fortex`/`foreg` are emacs-batch scripts driving `Fortify/fortify.el`), `ocaml-nox` (apt, for the 2012 spec's BNF preprocessor), and **stmaryrd** installed manually from CTAN tlnet archive into `/usr/local/share/texmf` + `updmap-sys` (avoids the huge texlive-fonts-extra). ~2 GB disk total.

**ONE TRACKED-FILE EDIT (prominent):** appended 14 lines to `/home/user/fortress/Fortify/fortify.sty` — `\providecommand` definitions for `\inclusiveprefix`, `\inclusivesuffix`, `\exclusiveprefix`, `\exclusivesuffix`, `\comprehensiveprefix`, `\comprehensivesuffix` (rendered as the base operator glyph with a small "PREFIX" etc. tag). Genuine 2012 bit-rot: `fortify.el` emits these for operator names like `opr PREFIX_SUM` (FortressLibrary.fsi:2535, CompilerLibrary), but no definition exists anywhere in the repo **or in its entire git history** — the 2012 spec build was already broken this way. Without it pdflatex dies at `\inclusiveprefix{\sum}` (page ~294). Not committed. Also note: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/{EllipsesNode,TemplateGapClass,TransformationNode}.java` show as modified in `git status` — **pre-existing dirt from before this task, not mine.**

### Target 1 — Specification/ (main spec): BUILT OK
- `cd Specification/fortress && ant genSource && ant tex` (env: JDK 25, `FORTRESS_HOME=/home/user/fortress`, `$FORTRESS_HOME/bin` on PATH, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS` unset). genSource ran perl scripts + foreg/fortex over 135 SpecData examples and 58 library `.fsi` files (~36 s); no interpreter evaluation needed (`tex` target skips `evalExs`).
- Output: `/home/user/fortress/Specification/fortress/fortress.pdf` — **589 pages**, title "The Fortress Language Specification — Working Draft — SVN Revision 4267". Zero undefined refs/citations.
- Committed `Specification/fortress.1.0.pdf` and `Specification-1.0-frozen/fortress.1.0.pdf` are **byte-equivalent metadata: both pdfeTeX-1.304, CreationDate 2008-03-31, 262 pages** — i.e., the published Version 1.0 PDF (March 2008). The fresh build (589 pp, r4267) is indeed the much richer post-1.0 working draft.

### Target 2 — Papers/Dispatch: BUILT OK
- Paper: **"Implementing Fully Modular, Statically Typed, Symmetric Multimethod Dispatch"** — Guy L. Steele Jr., David Chase, Eric Allen, Victor Luchangco (Oracle Labs), Sukyoung Ryu (KAIST). POPL 2011 *submission* (committed `SteelePOPL2011.pdf` is dvipdfm 0.13.2d, 2010-07-13, 12 pp two-column; `POPL-2011-response.txt` is the author response — apparently not accepted at POPL).
- Built via `make complete` (fortick → latex → bibtex → latex ×2 → dvipdfm). Output: `/home/user/fortress/Papers/Dispatch/main.pdf` — **21 pages** (sigplanconf `preprint` mode). One wrinkle: `main.tex` says `\bibliography{books}` but cites `traits`/`traitsOOPSLA04` which live only in `main.bib`; I rebuilt against the **committed** `main.bbl` (which has them) so all citations resolve, then `git checkout`-restored the tracked `main.aux/main.bbl/main.blg`. No source edits.

### Target 3 — Documentation/Specification: BUILT OK
- This is the **2012 ground-up rewrite of the spec** ("The Fortress Language Specification", dated by build day; committed `fortress.pdf` = pdfTeX-1.40.9, 2012-05-31, 65 pp). Tick-based, with an OCaml BNF grammar preprocessor.
- Built via `cd Documentation/Specification/Root && ant tex` (needs ocaml/ocamlc + emacs + perl). Output: `/home/user/fortress/Documentation/Specification/Generated/Root/fortress.pdf` — **66 pages** (I used `tex`, not the default `spec` target, deliberately: `spec` copies the PDF over the tracked committed one). ~26 dangling `??` cross-references to never-written sections — **the committed May 2012 PDF has 42 `??` too**; the draft is simply unfinished.

### Expanded scope — Papers/
1. **Papers/Types: BUILT OK.** "Type Checking Modular Multiple Dispatch with Parametric Polymorphism and Multiple Inheritance" — Eric Allen, Justin Hilburn, Scott Kilpatrick, Victor Luchangco; `\conferenceinfo{OOPSLA '11}{October 22–27, 2011, Portland, Oregon}`. `make all` (fortick+pdflatex+bibtex).
